titel: 453. 7 facts you need to know about your brain

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen (Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst podtrac.com) - zu wenig fuer ein Urteil, aber nicht nichts; Ausschnitte dieser Sendung waren in zwei Messungen mit Stunden Abstand stumm - die Datei wird je Abruf neu zusammengesetzt

einzeiler: Seven surprising and scientifically backed facts about how the human brain actually works.
kurzfassung: The episode explores seven lesser-known facts about brain function, debunking common myths about multitasking and brain capacity. It highlights how the brain physically rewires itself, processes emotional pain identically to physical pain, and maintains a deep connection with the gut. Additionally, it examines lifelong neural development and the crucial biological role of forgetting.
stichpunkte: Neuroplasticity allows the brain to reorganize structures and create new neural pathways throughout life.
Emotional rejection activates the same anterior insula and cingulate cortex regions as physical pain.
Humans use 100 percent of their brain, disproving the persistent ten percent myth originating from the 1890s.
The gut-brain axis connects the enteric nervous system directly to mood regulation and pain perception.
Multitasking incurs a cognitive cost, with studies showing 98 percent of people are ineffective at task-switching.
Brain development continues past age twenty-five, with major structural shifts occurring into early adulthood and the thirties.
Forgetting is an active, vital biological process driven by proteins like Musashi that clear space for new memories.

clips.text: An explanation of why people easily recall memories from over a decade ago while failing to remember meals from the previous day.

beschreibung:
There are a surprising number of myths and misconceptions about the brain, particularly with regards to its development in our 20s. In this episode, we unpack a number of surprising facts and studies about the brain so that we can in turn better understand how to make the most of our 20s.
Watch on Netflix: HERE
We unpack:
• The science of neuroplasticity and how our brain can rewire itself
• Why, on a cognitive level, a broken heart may not be so different from a broken arm
• How much of our brains we really use (hint - it’s more than 10%!)
• The gut-brain axis and why poor gut health can cause depression - not the other way around
• Why our brain needs to forget to function properly
• The real age our brain stops developing
